metadata.case_name: LAU CHUNG NAM v. AU WAI MAN

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: placement in a sheltered workshop for one year then simple non-intellectually demanding work

injuries.description: He was found to have sustained a severe head injury with radiological investigation revealing a right intercerebral haemorrhage and a left frontal epidural haematoma as well as a right frontal cerebral contusion.
source: He was found to have sustained a severe head injury with radiological investigation revealing a right intercerebral haemorrhage and a left frontal epidural haematoma as well as a right frontal cerebral contusion.
The plaintiff was then found to have persistent elevated intracranial pressure and a further operation for right frontal lobectomy was performed the next day.
Dr Choa was of the opinion that the plaintiff sustained a serious cerebral injury in the accident and which necessitated the removal of part of his right frontal lobe.

injuries.description: He also suffered a fractured cervical spine at the C3 spinal process.
source: He also suffered a fractured cervical spine at the C3 spinal process.
The fracture to his spinal process at C3 was treated conservatively.
Dr Lau was also of the view that the fracture to the spinal process at C3 has completely recovered.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of other specified cervical vertebra

injuries.description: There was a comminuted fracture of his left tibia and fibula.
source: There was a comminuted fracture of his left tibia and fibula.
Emergency operation for evacuation of epidural haematoma and for closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula was performed on the plaintiff the same day.

Dr Lau Hoi Kuen whose report dated 24 November 2001 stated that the plaintiff had made an excellent recovery from his fracture to the left tibia and fibula and that the range of movement of his left knee and ankle joint is well preserved.

injuries.description: Since that time, he has had regular epileptic seizures and convulsions; the plaintiff has post-traumatic epilepsy and his major handicap is his uncontrolled epilepsy.
source: Since that time, he has had regular epileptic seizures and convulsions, very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder.
Dr Choa was of the opinion that the plaintiff sustained a serious cerebral injury in the accident ... However, his major handicap is his uncontrolled epilepsy.
Dr Woo agrees that the plaintiff has post-traumatic epilepsy, headaches and subjective memory loss.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: Very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder.
source: Since that time, he has had regular epileptic seizures and convulsions, very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder. When that happened he had to be hospitalized for two to three days each time.
Dr Lau agrees with Dr Brian Choa that the plaintiff's main handicap is his uncontrolled epilepsy with the repeated dislocation to his left shoulder.
Although he found the shoulder to be normal when he examined the plaintiff, he commented that it could become unstable with recurrent dislocation if the epilepsy remains uncontrolled.

injuries.description: Moderate degree of cognitive impairment / cognitive deficits, mildly impaired intelligence, mildly impaired attention and visual memory; moderate cognitive impairment resulting from the head injury.
source: When first admitted to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation, the plaintiff was disorientated, still in post-traumatic amnesic phase and non-communicative showing non-purposeful movements of limbs.
Full cognitive assessment in mid-June showed mildly impaired intelligence, mildly impaired attention and visual memory.
Professor Lee ... concluded ... he still has unresolved post-traumatic epilepsy and a moderate degree of cognitive impairment.

Dr Lau further states that although orthopaedically there should be nothing preventing the plaintiff from returning to his pre-accident work as a cook, in fact he cannot do so because of the permanent cognitive impairment resulting from the head injury.

manifestations.description: Unconscious when first arrived at Tuen Mun Hospital; lost consciousness after being hit.
Post-traumatic amnesic phase, disorientation and non-communicative showing non-purposeful movements of limbs.
Motor power of the left limbs reduced to grade three out of five and tightness of left finger flexors.
Very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder.
Mild emotional lability in the form of inappropriate mirth; behavioural regression.
Not allowed to go out on his own and requires supervision because of epilepsy.

treatments_received: closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula
bone grafting and adjustment of external fixation (4 July 2000)
consultation with neurologist Dr Jason Fong and introduction of Tripleptal (December 2002)
treatments_future: trial of newer antiepileptic drugs in private practice
epilepsy surgery if newer drugs fail
rehabilitation/training in a sheltered workshop for one year before open employment

losses.description: Because of his epilepsy the plaintiff is not allowed to go out on his own thus his repertoire of social and leisure activities have narrowed significantly and he has not been in contact with his previous friends.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: His social and leisure activities have been significantly reduced.

Although orthopaedically there should be nothing preventing the plaintiff from returning to his pre-accident work as a cook, in fact he cannot do so because of the permanent cognitive impairment resulting from the head injury.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Because of his epilepsy the plaintiff is not allowed to go out on his own.
The plaintiff has moderate degree of cognitive impairment with mildly impaired intelligence, attention and visual memory.
